items: The first episode of Doctor Who was broadcast on 23 November 1963.
Coronation Street first aired on 9 December 1960 and is often called the world's longest-running TV soap.
“Wings” won Best Picture at the first Academy Awards ceremony, held in 1929.
The Simpsons began as short cartoons on The Tracey Ullman Show before getting their own series in 1989.
Toy Story (1995) was the first feature-length film made entirely with computer animation.
The Oscar statuette's official name is the Academy Award of Merit.
The BBC Television Service began regular broadcasts from Alexandra Palace in 1936.
The first programme shown on Channel 4, on 2 November 1982, was Countdown.
Blue Peter first aired in 1958 and is the world's longest-running children's TV show.
The Hollywood sign originally read “Hollywoodland” when it went up in 1923.
Sean Connery played James Bond in the first Bond film, Dr. No, which premiered in London in 1962.
Friends ran for ten series, from 1994 to 2004.
Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? first aired on ITV in 1998.
Wallace and Gromit were created by Nick Park at Aardman Animations in Bristol.
Desert Island Discs was first broadcast in 1942 and is one of the longest-running radio programmes in the world.
